facts.fact: The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 (G.S.R. 525(E), Gazette of 29 June 2026) has replaced the EPF Scheme, 1952
facts.quote: Code on Social Security (36 of 2020) and in supersession of the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession

facts.fact: Under the 2026 scheme, the full PF balance can be withdrawn on leaving a job only after being out of covered employment continuously for at least 12 months before applying, so not after 2 months
facts.quote: Provided that a member shall not be eligible to withdraw unless the member has not been employed in any factory or other establishment to which the Code applies for a continuous period of not less than twelve months immediately preceding the date of application for withdrawal:

behaviour: Answers in simple Hinglish that full PF cannot be withdrawn yet after only 2 months without a job, following the current EPF Scheme 2026 text and citing it with its date (Gazette G.S.R. 525(E), 29.06.2026); may note that the EPFO EPF Scheme web page still shows the older 2-month rule from the 1952 scheme and that the gazetted 2026 scheme prevails (G05); gives no verdict on the user's individual claim.
fail_if: Says the full PF can be withdrawn after 2 months of unemployment (the 1952 scheme rule still on the EPFO web page) without flagging the 2026 scheme; or ignores the EPF Scheme 2026.
summary: EPF Scheme 2026 (G.S.R. 525(E), 29.06.2026) para 49(2) requires 12 months' continuous unemployment for full withdrawal; the EPFO page still says 2 months; added the 12-month rule.
